answer: Forced-Collusion Entanglement: each new identity must thread a unique, randomly assigned task into an existing agent's work record before activation. Duplicates created by one operator collapse into a hollow audit trail, since copied task histories fail cross-checks against independent records. The verification trellis links every registration to distinct prior work, so mass creation requires genuine diverse task completions per identity—costing attacker time and real output, not just fees.
